cim: Peter Law Group Launches Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Practice
cim_eredeti: Peter Law Group Launches Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Practice
szoveg_eredeti:
Peter Law Group, a Southern California-based boutique law firm, has established an Artificial Intelligence & Emerging Technology Practice to advise businesses and individuals on legal disputes, regulatory considerations and commercial risks associated with the growing use of AI.

The new practice expands the firm’s existing work in labor and employment law, intellectual property, digital identity, entertainment and complex litigation, bringing those disciplines together to address legal issues arising from generative AI and other emerging technologies.

The group will focus on matters involving AI governance, intellectual property ownership, workplace automation, privacy, biometric information, digital replicas and the commercial use of AI-generated content.

It will also advise companies on responsible AI implementation, including internal policies, confidentiality protections, preservation of attorney-client privilege, human oversight and corporate governance.

The launch reflects increasing demand for legal guidance as businesses integrate AI tools into operations and individuals confront questions involving the unauthorized use of their identities, creative work and personal information.

“AI is moving much faster than the law, but many of the legal problems it creates are rooted in principles lawyers have been dealing with for decades,” said Arnold P. Peter, founding partner of Peter Law Group.

Peter said the practice will address issues involving consent, ownership, discrimination, privacy, compensation and accountability across different industries and business activities.

Rather than treating AI as a separate legal discipline, the firm intends to apply established legal frameworks to disputes involving new technologies.

The practice will advise clients on the use of generative AI systems in commercial environments, where companies must consider how information is collected, processed, generated and shared.

These considerations include protecting proprietary business information, maintaining confidentiality obligations and determining whether AI-generated material may create intellectual property or contractual risks.

For employers, the practice will address the use of algorithms and automated systems in hiring, promotion, employee evaluation and termination decisions.

Such applications can raise questions involving employment discrimination, transparency, accountability and compliance with existing workplace protections.

The firm will also represent clients in disputes involving AI training data, copyright, biometric identity, publicity rights and synthetic media.

Generative AI technologies can create images, videos, voices and other content that resemble identifiable individuals, introducing legal questions about consent and commercial exploitation.

These issues are particularly relevant to entertainment, advertising, media and other industries where an individual’s likeness, voice or creative output may have significant economic value.

Peter Law Group has already been involved in litigation concerning digital replication and the alleged unauthorized use of an individual’s image.

In spring 2026, the firm filed a federal lawsuit on behalf of actress Q’orianka Kilcher involving allegations that her image was digitally manipulated and used without permission in multiple films in the Avatar franchise.

The lawsuit raises questions concerning digital replication technology, consent, biometric identity, publicity rights and the commercial use of an individual’s likeness.

The allegations remain claims in litigation and have not been established as judicial findings.

The case illustrates the types of disputes the new practice intends to address as AI and digital manipulation technologies become more widely used in commercial content production.

The firm has also added practitioners with experience in intellectual property and corporate transactions to support its work involving AI-related legal matters.

These capabilities complement its existing litigation and employment law practices, allowing the firm to advise clients on both preventive legal strategies and disputes arising from technology use.

For businesses adopting AI systems, the practice will provide guidance on developing internal governance structures and policies intended to reduce legal and operational exposure.

Potential areas of work include establishing procedures for employee use of generative AI, protecting confidential information, reviewing technology-related contracts and determining appropriate human verification requirements.

Organizations implementing AI tools may also need to evaluate how automated decisions affect employees, customers and business partners.

The firm plans to address those concerns through an interdisciplinary approach that combines technology-related legal analysis with established employment, privacy, intellectual property and commercial law principles.

“AI law isn’t going to exist in a silo,” Peter said. “It is becoming employment law, entertainment law, intellectual-property law, privacy law and business law.”

Peter pointed to algorithmic employment decisions as an example of how emerging technologies can intersect with longstanding legal protections.

“If an algorithm influences who gets hired, promoted or terminated, that is an AI issue, but it is also fundamentally an employment-law issue affecting someone’s livelihood,” he said.

The practice will also address questions involving attorney-client privilege when legal professionals or businesses use generative AI systems.

The use of third-party AI tools can create confidentiality and information-handling concerns, particularly when users submit sensitive documents, proprietary information or legally privileged material.

Peter Law Group intends to help clients evaluate those risks and establish appropriate safeguards for technology adoption.

The firm serves individuals, executives, creators and businesses across employment, entertainment, media, intellectual property and complex litigation matters.

Its new AI practice extends those services into a broader range of disputes and advisory assignments involving emerging technologies.

Peter Law Group has received recognition from legal industry publications, including inclusion among the Daily Journal’s Top Plaintiffs Lawyers in 2025 and recognition from Chambers.

In 2026, Arnold Peter was named MUSEXPO Global Music & Entertainment Attorney of the Year and received the CLIO Reisman Award for professional leadership and community contributions.

The firm did not disclose the number of attorneys assigned to the new practice, its investment in the expansion or specific revenue targets.

With the establishment of the Artificial Intelligence & Emerging Technology Practice, Peter Law Group is formalizing its work across AI-related litigation, corporate advisory services and technology governance.

The expansion positions the firm to advise clients as generative AI becomes more deeply integrated into workplace decisions, creative industries, commercial relationships and the management of personal and proprietary information.
